Briefly describe analytical chemistry, medicinal chemistry and inorganic chemistry.
keyPoints: ["Analytical chemistry: methods and instruments for composition and properties","Medicinal chemistry: drugs, biological targets, and medicinal agents","Inorganic chemistry: elements and compounds except organic compounds"]
modelAnswer: Analytical chemistry uses methods and instruments to determine the composition and properties of matter. Medicinal chemistry studies interactions between drugs and biological targets and develops new medicinal agents. Inorganic chemistry deals with elements and their compounds except organic compounds.

stem: Briefly describe nuclear chemistry, environmental chemistry and astrochemistry.
keyPoints: ["Nuclear chemistry: changes in atomic nuclei","Environmental chemistry: pollutants and adverse effects","Astrochemistry: chemical processes in astronomical environments"]
modelAnswer: Nuclear chemistry studies changes that occur in atomic nuclei. Environmental chemistry studies chemical and toxic substances that pollute the environment and their adverse effects on people. Astrochemistry studies chemical processes and reactions in astronomical environments such as stars, planets, comets, and interstellar space.

stem: Define astrochemistry, geochemistry, physical chemistry.
keyPoints: ["Astrochemistry: astronomical chemical processes","Geochemistry: Earth materials and elemental distribution","Physical chemistry: laws and theories of matter"]
modelAnswer: Astrochemistry studies chemical processes and reactions in astronomical environments. Geochemistry studies the chemical composition, distribution, and transformation of elements and compounds in the Earth's crust, including rocks, minerals, soils, water, and the atmosphere. Physical chemistry uses laws and theories to understand the structure and changes of matter.
